main_text.p: Est imperium ad utilitatem multorum, scilicet tenuiorum spectans: qualem statum somniabat An-no Christi 1525. Germanica plebs in tumultu rusti-corum.
Lecturus praecepta prolixiora videat Politica Ari-stotelis, & Thomae Freigii Quaestiones politicas.
Hactenus est Politica declarata: sequitur de Apo-demica.
main_text.head: DE APODEMICA.
main_text.p: APODEMICA, die reisekunst/ est ars bene peregrinandi ad consequendam politicam rerum cognitionem. Haec cognitio consistit in regionibus, urbibus, politia, & incolis cognoscendis.

Tria: aër, aqua, terra. Aër, utrùm salubris an pesti-lens sit, qui venti, quae aves, quae infecta. In aqua con-sideranda, Flumina perpetua, torrentes, lacus, balneae, thermae, piscinae, fontes, rivi, aquaeductus.
In terra sunt consideranda, Agri, pagi, vici, arces, fodinae, metalla, frumenta, plantae, villae, animantia domestica & fera, frequentia urbium, res gestae, ap-pellatio.
Ambitus, der[?] umbkreis / centrum, das mittel in der Statt / & radii, die strassen. In ambitu seu circuitu sunt navalia, portus, portae, carceres & muri. Centrum

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of the lines, so the last words of several lines are missing or partly visible (for example "scilicet", "balneae", "arces", "ap-", "Centrum"). These are not transcribed beyond what is visible. The first word of "der umbkreis" is printed in black letter and reads as "ber" in the scan; it is marked [?] as probably "der". The woodcut initial A joins to "PODEMICA" as "APODEMICA". The word "est" at the bottom right is a catchword and is not repeated in the text. Printed slashes are kept as they stand. Black letter is used for German words.
